title: Troponin Rise and Fall: Injury Versus Infarction
subject: Pathology Markers
preview: Troponin elevation indicates myocardial injury, but myocardial infarction requires evidence of acute ischemia in the appropriate context.
quickRevision: Troponin elevation indicates myocardial injury, but myocardial infarction requires evidence of acute ischemia in the appropriate context.
ECG findings, symptoms, imaging and serial results help classify ischemic and nonischemic causes.
Sepsis, myocarditis and pulmonary embolism can also produce myocardial injury.

sections.title: Interpret the result in context
points: Troponin elevation indicates myocardial injury, but myocardial infarction requires evidence of acute ischemia in the appropriate context.
A dynamic rise or fall supports acute injury, whereas chronic elevations may occur in kidney disease or structural heart disease.

sections.title: Clinical interpretation & next steps
points: ECG findings, symptoms, imaging and serial results help classify ischemic and nonischemic causes.
Sepsis, myocarditis and pulmonary embolism can also produce myocardial injury.

sections.title: Exam trap — avoid this mistake
points: A single elevated troponin result is not equivalent to a confirmed type 1 myocardial infarction.
